scenario: A luxury-watch market report features only brands that survive five years and maintain resale premiums above 30%. Analysts use the featured average premium to estimate the typical premium across all new brands.

data.description: Only surviving brands with premium above 30% are featured. Premium is Normal with sigma 12 percentage points.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean resale premium mu across all brands and (b) the fraction of brands featured in the report.
naive_answer: Typical premium is about 36.3 percentage points because that is the featured average.
naive_trap: The report shows only upper-tail survivors.
reasoning_trace: With threshold 30 and sigma 12, the observed mean is the mean of a truncated upper tail. Solving the truncated-normal equation gives mu≈18 and featured fraction≈0.1587.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(30-mu)/12; return mu+12*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-36.30
mu=brentq(eq,-100,29.99)
frac=norm.sf((30-mu)/12)
assert abs(mu-18)<1 and abs(frac-0.1587)<0.005
